name: process.list
description: Enumerate running processes. Returns pid, ppid, and image name per entry, sorted alphabetically by image name. Session-0 service processes are excluded by default (`include_system: true` to restore). Pass `include_counters: true` to add CPU/memory/handle counts. Read-only.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against the image name (e.g. `notepad` matches `Notepad.exe`). Omit to list all processes.

include_counters.description: If true, each entry adds resource counters: CPU%, RSS, working set, private bytes, thread count, handle count, start time. Adds modest cost (per-pid OpenProcess + GetProcessTimes + GetProcessMemoryInfo + GetProcessHandleCount), so opt-in.

limit.description: Cap on the number of processes returned after filtering and sorting. Default 100. Use `pattern` to narrow results on machines with many processes (developer machines commonly have 200–300+).

include_system.description: When false (default), session-0 processes (Windows service host session) are excluded. Session-0 contains background services (antivirus, audio, VPN) that are rarely relevant to interactive agent tasks. Pass `include_system: true` to include them. Requires one `ProcessIdToSessionId` call per snapshot entry.

image.description: Executable name (filename without path), e.g. `Notepad.exe`. Empty string for kernel-internal processes the agent can't query.

ppid.description: Parent process id. May be 0 or refer to a no-longer-running process if the parent has exited.

cpu_percent.description: CPU usage as a percentage of one core (0.0–100.0 per core; multi-core processes can exceed 100). Computed over a short sampling interval at the snapshot moment. Only present when `include_counters: true`.

rss_bytes.description: Resident set size — physical memory currently in RAM (Win32 `WorkingSetSize` from PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS). Only present when `include_counters: true`.

working_set_bytes.description: Same as `rss_bytes` on Windows; preserved for cross-platform clarity. Only present when `include_counters: true`.

private_bytes.description: Private (non-shared) memory committed for the process (Win32 `PagefileUsage` from PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX). Only present when `include_counters: true`.

thread_count.description: Number of threads currently in the process. Only present when `include_counters: true`.

handle_count.description: Number of open Win32 handles (Win32 `GetProcessHandleCount`). Only present when `include_counters: true`.

start_time_unix_s.description: Process start time as Unix epoch seconds (Win32 `GetProcessTimes.lpCreationTime` converted from FILETIME). Only present when `include_counters: true`.

x-implementations.name: create_toolhelp32_snapshot
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS)` + `Process32FirstW` / `Process32NextW` walk. Each PROCESSENTRY32W carries th32ProcessID, th32ParentProcessID, and szExeFile. With `include_counters`, the agent additionally calls OpenProcess + GetProcessTimes + GetProcessMemoryInfo + GetProcessHandleCount per entry.

x-implementations.name: enum_processes
x-implementations.description: Win32 `EnumProcesses` + `OpenProcess` + `GetModuleBaseNameW` per pid. More verbose, sometimes catches edge cases Toolhelp misses. Same per-pid counter calls under `include_counters`.

windows-modern.description: CreateToolhelp32Snapshot is the primary path; falls back to EnumProcesses + GetModuleBaseName when Toolhelp fails (rare). Filter applied client-side after enumeration. Per-process reads of image name may fail with ERR permission_denied for protected processes (anti-cheat / antivirus); those entries report `image: ""`. With `include_counters`, protected processes also have empty/zero counter fields when OpenProcess fails for them.

windows-classic.description: CreateToolhelp32Snapshot on NT 5+ and Win 9x (kernel32 export). NT 4 lacks Toolhelp in kernel32; the agent loads PSAPI.DLL and uses EnumProcesses on NT 4. With `include_counters`, GetProcessHandleCount is NT 5.1+ — pre-XP agents return 0 for `handle_count`.
